analysis.title: GS - McCarthy - IG Credit Week in Review - 8 Nov 2026
key_insights: IG issuance was $76bn last week, the 4th largest week of 2026 and the largest November week ever. Total US IG debt issuance is a record $2.079tn YTD.
Credit held up during Thursday's equity selloff. NDX fell 6.4% and SPX fell 4.4% while CDXIG widened only 3.5bps.
Hyperscaler debt financing remains the dominant focus. GIR notes five separate hyperscaler bond deals since Oct 29 totaling $67bn.
Investors are demanding elevated new issue concessions for AI issuers versus the non-AI cohort, but supply keeps coming to market.

The latest AI issuance is shifting shorter in duration. META issued only $2.75bn of 30yr bonds out of a $15bn deal and brought no 40yr for the first time. ORCL's $10bn deal had no 30yr or 40yr, with a $1.5bn 20yr as the longest bond. AAPL issued $7.5bn with no 30yr.

The GS hyperscaler 30yr basket has flattened vs the 10yr basket by about 25%. The 10s30s spread moved from 40bps at the steepest to 31bps, while the non-AI 10s30s curve is little changed over three months.
Expected growth in chip financing as a share of AI-related issuance in 2027 is another technical flattening hyperscaler curves.
A basket of Chip CDS now trades wider than a basket of Hyperscaler CDS for the first time in three months. Chip CDS has underperformed its relative beta over the past two months.
AI CDS volumes keep climbing. Excluding the September semi-annual roll, the past two weeks were the most active ever at 8-10bn of AI CDS traded per week.

sector_views.rationale: Supply is heavy and new issue concessions are elevated versus non-AI, but credit spreads stayed stable through the equity selloff. The note describes market technicals rather than a directional call.

risk_factors: Continued heavy hyperscaler issuance with elevated new issue concessions.
Expected growth in chip financing in 2027 may add supply and pressure chip credit spreads.
Equity volatility in the AI universe, which has so far not spread to credit.

Chart showing a basket of Chip CDS trading wider than a basket of Hyperscaler CDS for the first time in three months (GS FICC and Equities, as of 11/6/26).
vol_and_positioning: CDXIG widened only 3.5bps on Thursday while NDX fell 6.4% and SPX fell 4.4%.
Chip CDS now trades wider than Hyperscaler CDS for the first time in three months.
AI CDS volume has run at 8-10bn per week for the past two weeks, the most active on record excluding the September roll.
geopolitical: U.S. midterm election results were cited as one of the events the market digested last week.
